sections.sectionText: Experiments are performed on aqueous corrosion, identification of oxidation products of titanium alloys, and casting and characterization of binary Al-Si alloys. The course emphasizes alloy design principles, the proper use of instrumentation for techniques such as optical and scanning electron microscopy, electrodynamic polarization, and x-ray diffraction, as well as communication skills, and the importance of safety.

sections.sectionText: Predicting elastic behavior from atomic bonding in crystal, and microstructure in composites. Hands-on experience with popular microscopic computational materials science and engineering software through project-based learning in electronic structure calculation (Quantum Espresso) and finite element modeling (OOF2). Students will also develop proficiency in the command line interface and bash shell scripting. The course will prioritize the physical principles underlying the software to confer an understanding of their applicability and limitations, and hands-on immersive praxis to give students the confidence and expertise to independently use these tools.

restrictions: Restricted to students in the Materials Science & Engineerng department.
sections.sectionText: Exploration of emerging materials of reduced dimensionality through hands-on experiments. Students learn to handle/process atomically thin materials such as graphene, fabricate field-effect transistors from these materials, and carry out various means of characterization including electrical, Raman, and optical measurements. In addition, effects of external stimuli (e.g., mechanical and chemical) on electrical characteristics are also examined.

sections.sectionText: Experiments are performed on time-temperature-transformations of steel, rolling and recrystallization of brass, and heat treatment of Al alloys. The course emphasizes physical metallurgy through experimentation, the proper use of instrumentation for metallographic preparation, hardness and tensile testing, and optical and scanning electron microscopy, as well as communication skills, and the importance of safety.

restrictions: Restricted to students in the Materials Science & Engineerng department.
sections.sectionText: Students are introduced to emerging photovoltaic materials through hands-on experiments. Students fabricate and characterize solar cells made of materials such as organometal halide perovskites. Different methods to synthesize/deposit these materials and device architectures are examined. Students then critically examine advantages and challenges associated with integrating new materials into photovoltaics.

sections.sectionText: Predicting plastic behavior from dislocation behavior and interaction in metals. Hands-on experience with popular macroscopic computational materials science and engineering software through project-based learning in molecular simulation (LAMMPS) and discrete dislocation dynamics (ParaDiS). Students will also develop proficiency in data analysis and visualization in MATLAB. The course will prioritize the physical principles underlying the software to confer an understanding of their applicability and limitations, and hands-on immersive praxis to give students the confidence and expertise to independently use these tools.

In this lab module, students will study the control of the quantum states of an ensemble of NV- defects in diamond, use pulsed sequences to determine the longitudinal and transverse relaxation times of the defect, and design pulse sequences to control the sensitivity of the NV- defect to temperature and magnetic field.

sections.sectionText: Meets with ME 598 (48380) and CSE 498 (70543). We introduce the connection of materials and data science, and specific issues regarding experimental and computational materials data. Topics include data acquisition and management, data curation, uncertainty quantification, and applying machine learning to materials data. The focus will be on current scientific literature in the emerging materials and data area.

sections.sectionText: This course will provide students with an in-depth understanding of Material Informatics and Accelerated Characterization, focusing on how these advanced techniques can be used to expedite the development and deployment of new materials. Students will gain experience with various computational tools and advanced characterization techniques.
